thread:
tom: Hey everyone 1 planning to relocate my primary home base from CA to Dublin, Ireland around Sept 1. Want to understand payroll switch, WFH stipend changes, and any tax/equity implications for my RSUs/ISO exercise windows. Is this straightforward?

maria (People Ops): @tom big question 1 are you moving permanently (change of legal home base) or temporary? That determines payroll cutover vs remote-work temporary policies.

tom: Permanent. Family move, kids school. I'll be a full-time Redwood employee and want to stay on company headcount.

chris (Payroll): For a permanent move we generally need to transition payroll to the Ireland payroll/legal entity or run a cross-border payroll arrangement. That affects withholding, social contributions, and pension scheme. We'll need your official move date, Irish address, and start/end dates for CA payroll.

emma (Legal): Also confirm citizenship/visas. If you become Irish tax resident, local employment law may apply (notice periods, statutory benefits). We must also check employment contract wording re: place of work and local mandatory terms. Don't sign anything until we update contract/terms if needed.

jess (Compensation): Equity note: moving jurisdictions can change tax treatment for RSUs/ISOs on vest/exercise. Ireland has different withholding and tax deferral options. For ISOs, US-specific tax treatment might be impacted if you cease US residency. We'll run a benefits/equity review and advise on safe timing for any planned exercises.

nina (Manager): Team supports the move. If Payroll/People Ops need a manager attestation about duties/location, I'll provide it.

maria (People Ops): Action items for @tom: 1) complete the relocation intention form: https://go.redwoodinference.com/relocate 2) upload ID and new address once you have it 3) choose preferred payroll outcome (a) move to Ireland payroll (recommended for permanency) or (b) remain on US payroll with cross-border payroll services (short-term only).

tom: Form submitted (link confirmation). Preferred: move to Ireland payroll. Move date Sept 1. New address added. US leave date Aug 31.

chris (Payroll): Received. We'll run an Ireland payroll setup checklist: registration, tax numbers (PPS?), PAYE setup, employer social contributions, and benefits enrollment mapping. Expect initial guidance in 5 business days and likely an HR-led employment addendum.

emma (Legal): We'll draft an amendment to your contract with place-of-work and statutory notices for Ireland. Also will coordinate with comp on equity language.

jess (Compensation): Quick interim guidance: avoid exercising ISOs within 60 days of payroll change without checking tax impact. We'll prepare a memo on RSU withholding and potential double-tax credit filing.

maria (People Ops): WFH stipend: once Ireland is your primary work location the US home-office stipend will stop. We have an Ireland-appropriate home setup allowance policy; amounts and timing differ. We'll share the country-specific policy doc.

hr-bot: Reminder: enroll in relocation assistance portal (relocate.redwood) to request shipping, house-hunting stipend, and moving-day support.

chris (Payroll): Also: benefits (health/dental) transfer may be impacted. Some benefits are US-only; we'll map equivalent Irish offerings or provide cost-neutral transitional benefits for a short period.

emma (Legal): Visas/permits: if you're not an EU/Irish citizen, please confirm visa status ASAP. If Redwood will sponsor work authorization, that adds lead time.

tom: I'm a US/Irish dual citizen, so no visa needed.

maria (People Ops): Great. Timeline: payroll/comp/legal review and draft addendum by EOD next week. We'll loop you for signatures and a benefits briefing. Marking status: "relocation onboarding started".

tom: Thanks all 1 appreciate the clear next steps. Happy to jump on a call if needed.

nina (Manager): I'll join any call and provide context on role continuity. :thumbsup:
